resale_co.name: Camden Resale Occupancy Certificate (C.R.O.C.); formerly Certificate of Continued Occupancy (C.C.O.)
resale_co.issued_by: City of Camden Construction & Building Bureau (Department of Code Enforcement)
resale_co.lead_time: Zoning approval must be obtained first; no set number of days published
requirements: Zoning permit and zoning approval before the application is accepted
Building, electrical, plumbing and fire inspections by the Building Bureau
All open building permits must be closed before the inspection
General inspection of the visible parts of the building for Uniform Construction Code violations
Separate smoke/CO certificate from the Fire Marshal (the $200 fee does not include the fire safety fee)

fees.label: C.R.O.C. application
fees.quote: The fee to apply for a C.R.O.C is $200.00. The fee DOES NOT include the Fire Safety fee of $64.00.

fees.label: Penalty if the buyer closes without the certificate (up to)
fees.quote: Penalties up to $2,000.00, may be levied by the Building Bureau.

resale_co.how_to_apply: First apply for a zoning permit (Zoning, City Hall Room 224, 856-757-7214). After zoning approval, submit the application to the Building Bureau, City Hall Room 403, 520 Market Street (856-757-7032). The seller is responsible for applying; the buyer may apply as the seller's agent with written permission, and the certificate is issued to the buyer. Building Bureau visits are by appointment only (call the day before) and permit applications and inspection requests go by email. The posted form is still the 2022 CCO application; no separate C.R.O.C. form was found.

evidence.quote: The City of Camden requires that a Camden Resale Occupancy Certificate shall be applied for and issued prior to the sale or conveyance of any property within the city.
The application is good for 6 months. After 6 months a new application must be filled out and paid for, unless there are open permits.
However, the certificate goes to the BUYER NOT THE SELLER.
Steps to obtain a C.C.O. which is optional and by request only
It is also necessary to “close out” all existing open permits prior to the CCO inspection.
It also handles all inspections for a Continued Certificate of Occupancy.

The owner of any residential property shall obtain an occupancy permit prior to the sale of such property involving a new occupancy of any unit of dwelling space, provided that no occupancy permit shall be required for the sale of vacant properties but shall be required at such time as a new occupancy occurs.

resale_co.notes: As of May 2025 the City's FAQ calls the required resale certificate a Camden Resale Occupancy Certificate (C.R.O.C.), $200, required before any sale or conveyance, and relabels the older Certificate of Continued Occupancy (C.C.O.) as 'optional and by request only'. An older FAQ entry on the same page still says a CCO is required before sale, and the Building Bureau still links only the 2022 CCO application (CCO FEE: $200.00, same amount). Treat the C.R.O.C. as the current requirement and confirm the form with the Building Bureau. The City code (read on ecode360) also requires an occupancy permit from Code Enforcement before the sale of residential property with a new occupancy (Section 620-39), and its fee tables list older amounts that do not match the City's pages (Section 620-22G: $75 selling fee; Chapter 270 fee table: 'Certificate of continued occupancy' $264). The City's own $200 is used here. If the property is not habitable, the buyer can sign an 'Agreement Not to Occupy' (https://www.camdennj.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/AGREEMENT-NOT-TO-OCCUPY-V05-2025.pdf). Rentals and tenant changes go through the Housing Department (856-757-7075), a separate program. Construction Official James Rizzo's email is from the Building Bureau contact directory (September 2026).

requirements: 10-year sealed battery smoke alarm on every level, or hardwired where required; hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery units
Smoke alarm on the ceiling in every bedroom
Basement alarm at the bottom of the stairwell on the ceiling (not between joists); hallway alarm within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
Hardwired smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
CO alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms; not in switched outlets or outlets at floor molding
Fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen in the path of exit, mounted on a bracket, minimum rating 2A-10B:C, under 10 pounds (form still lists it)
House numbers at least 4 inches, contrasting, fixed to the house and visible from the street (numbers on a light post or mailbox not accepted)
Monitored low-voltage fire alarm systems must be tested by an alarm contractor, with the certification given to the inspector

authorities.name: Camden Fire Department, Office of the Fire Marshal
authorities.lead_time: Submit the request 3 to 4 weeks before settlement; 8 or more calendar days ahead for the lowest fee. Certificates are valid for 90 days.

fees.label: Request received 8 or more calendar days before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received eight (8) calendar days or more prior to the settlement date: $64.00

fees.label: Request received with less notice (published as 'seven (7) calendar days or more')
fees.quote: Requests received seven (7) calendar days or more to the settlement date: $115.00

fees.label: Request received 3 calendar days or less before settlement
fees.quote: Requests received three (3) calendar days or less prior to the settlement date: $162.00

fees.label: Senior discount (sellers 62 and over, off the first inspection fee, proof of age required)
fees.quote: Sellers age 62 & over may deduct $30.00 from the first inspection fee

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Residential Inspection Request Form and email it to Raymond Barker (RaBarker@camdennj.gov) or call 856-757-7531. Pay by check or money order payable to 'Uniform Fire Safety Act' (UFSA) before the inspection, or mail it in advance to Camden Fire Department, Office of the Fire Marshal, 4 N. 3rd Street, Camden, NJ 08102. Cash is not accepted. Inspections are between 9:00 am and 3:00 pm.
authorities.contact_title: Chief Fire Marshal (Fire Official); resale requests go to Raymond Barker

fire_cert.notes: The 2025 request form and the 2024 requirements sheet list the same fees ($64.00, $115.00, $162.00; re-inspection $35.00). The middle tier is worded 'seven (7) calendar days or more' on the City sheet, which appears to mean 4 to 7 days; confirm with the Fire Marshal. The City code (Section 363-12, read on ecode360) still lists older amounts ($50, $100 and $140 by business days before settlement); the Fire Marshal's posted sheet and form amounts are used here. The 2024 requirements sheet still lists a fire extinguisher, which the state dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), while the 2025 request form names only smoke and carbon monoxide alarms; confirm whether the extinguisher is still checked. The C.R.O.C. FAQ says the building certificate fee does not include the $64.00 fire safety fee. The 2024 sheet says requests 'must be submitted using the online form located at ci.camden.nj.us'; the current site posts the request form as a PDF. Chief Fire Marshal Joseph Tull: JoTull@camdennj.gov.

other_items.label: Zoning approval first
other_items.detail: A zoning permit and approval are required before the Building Bureau accepts the CCO/C.R.O.C. application. Zoning: City Hall Room 224, 856-757-7214.

other_items.label: Open permits closed
other_items.detail: All existing open building permits must be closed out before the CCO inspection; no certificate is issued while permits are open.

open_questions: Is there a separate C.R.O.C. application form (only the 2022 CCO application is posted), and does the C.R.O.C. inspection scope differ from the old CCO?
Exact day range for the $115.00 fire tier (the City wording is ambiguous).
Does the Fire Marshal still require a fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19? The 2024 sheet lists one.
How long is the issued C.R.O.C. valid? Only the 6-month application window is stated.
